reason: Under 'Scan behaviors for Amazon ECR scanning' the quote says that on first activation Inspector detects images pushed within the last 14 days and scans them, only scans images with imageStatus ACTIVE, and does not scan ARCHIVED images.

The saved page lists 3, 7, 14 (default), 30, 60, 90, 180 days and Lifetime under the bold label 'Image push date duration', whose sentence says it sets how long Inspector monitors images after push; Lifetime appears only in that list (the re-scan list stops at 180 days).

The quotas row supports 10,000 member accounts per delegated administrator, based on Organizations quotas, but the qualifier adjustable: true (printed as 'adjustable' for a quota) is not stated anywhere in the quote or context; the row only lacks the 'cannot request an increase' note.

The overview quotes say you don't need to manually schedule or configure assessment scans, Inspector automatically discovers and begins scanning eligible resources, and rescans on changes such as a new package, a patch, or a newly published CVE affecting the resource.

The score page says Inspector determines the score by correlating CVSS base score information with network reachability and exploitability data, and the overview gives the EC2 example where the score may be lowered when no open network path to the internet exists.
The quotas page states 'Allow lists per account: 10, 1-5 ... predefined text and 1-5 ... regular expressions' and that unless otherwise noted each quota applies to your account in each Region.

Under 'Preventative control monitoring' the page lists S3 buckets per account: 10,000 and the quote describes full monitoring for the 10,000 most recently created or changed buckets and no evaluation, policy findings or complete inventory for the rest.

The quotas page states monthly analysis per account by sensitive data discovery jobs is 5 TB, applies only to those jobs, and can be increased to as much as 1,000 TB (1 PB) with the Service Quotas console.
The free trial page states the trial doesn't include analysis by sensitive data discovery jobs and charges apply for jobs that analyze more than 1 GB of uncompressed data during the trial.

The managed data identifiers page states the large and growing list and the three categories with exactly the examples in the claim (private keys, AWS secret access keys; credit card and bank account numbers; PHI and PII examples).

The overview states the two ways (Organizations or membership invitations), the administrator tasks (review member buckets, review policy findings, inspect buckets for sensitive data) and that with Organizations the administrator can also enable Macie for members.

The repository page states results are stored for only 90 days, long-term retention needs a KMS key and an S3 bucket, settings apply only to the current Region and only to the administrator's own account, and must be configured in each Region used.

Under 'Supported Amazon S3 storage classes' the page lists Glacier Instant Retrieval, Intelligent-Tiering and One Zone-IA among supported classes and states Macie doesn't analyze other classes such as Glacier Deep Archive or Express One Zone, nor objects in directory buckets.
The automation rules page states a rule applies only in the Region in which it's created and the administrator must create it in each Region to apply it in multiple Regions.

The case study states SMEJ Guardrail's foundation is AWS Security Hub, it also uses GuardDuty to monitor accounts for suspicious activities, and it is used across more than 300 AWS accounts and helps protect 1,300 websites.

The case study states Security Hub assesses resources against benchmarks such as CIS and AWS FSBP, the quote credits centralized management and visualization with standardizing security levels, and SMEJ Guardrail (built on Security Hub) maintains a uniform security layer across accounts.

The central configuration page states it requires integrating with Organizations, lets the delegated administrator enable Security Hub CSPM and configure standards and controls for accounts and OUs across Regions from a home Region, and uses configuration policies.

The prerequisites page states AWS Config must be enabled in each Region where Security Hub CSPM is enabled to receive control findings and, multi-account, in each Region for the administrator and all member accounts.

The integrations page states Config managed and custom rule evaluations appear as CSPM findings, are sent through EventBridge, only post-enablement evaluations are sent, and service-linked rule evaluations are excluded except Control Tower's.

The page states the current default standards are FSBP and CIS v1.2.0, local configuration can auto-enable them for new member accounts, turning that off is possible only with Organizations and local configuration, and central configuration uses a configuration policy instead.

The pricing page FAQ says the essentials plan combines Inspector and CSPM into a single resource-based pricing model, and the Benefits section names transitioning from usage-based to resource-based pricing with unlimited security checks and finding ingestions; the claim attributes it to the page as stated.

The introduction states CSPM uses service-linked Config rules for most controls and you must enable Config and record resources for most control findings; the checks page states other controls use custom Lambda functions managed by CSPM with no prerequisites.

The FAQ answer on enablement at GA states enabling Security Hub automatically enables CSPM, the next step uses console, policies or APIs to enable Inspector capabilities and GuardDuty-powered threat detection analytics, and Macie is not automatically enabled.

The Essentials plan section names a per-resource unit price and states per-resource pricing applies only to EC2 instances, ECR container images, Lambda functions, and IAM users and roles, with all other monitored resources included.

The free trial summary states a 30-day trial with Essentials plan capabilities for every account in each Region enabled with Security Hub, even after CSPM or Inspector trials, and excludes add-ons and the Extended plan.

The Security Hub introduction states it generates findings in OCSF and receives OCSF findings from Security Hub CSPM, GuardDuty, Macie and Inspector; the CSPM introduction states CSPM processes findings in ASFF.
